subject: general
question: A well of radius 2 m is dug 16.8 m deep. The soil taken out of it is spread evenly all around the well to form a 48 cm high embankment. What is the width (in m) of the embankment?
solution:
Given:

Inner radius 2 m

Height of the well = 16.8 m

Height of the embankment = 48 cm

 Concept used:

The volume of a cylinder = πr2h1 cubic units

Volume of a hollow cylinder = π(R2 - r2)h2 cubic units

R = outer radius,

r = inner radius, and

h1 = height of the cylinder

h2 = height of the embankment

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Calculation:

Let width of the embankment be x m

Here,

r = 2 m

h₁ = 16.8 m

R = (2 + x)

h₂ = 48 cm

Now,

According to the question,

πr2h1 = π(R2 - r2)h2

⇒ 2² × 16.8 = {(2 + x)2 - 22} × (48/100) [1 cm = 0.01 m]

⇒ (4 × 16.8 × 100)/48 = {(2 + x)2 - 22} 

⇒ 140 = 2² + x² + 2 × 2 × x - 2²

⇒ 140 = x2 + 4x

⇒ x2 + 4x - 140 = 0

⇒ x2 + 14x - 10x - 140 = 0

⇒ x(x + 14) - 10(x + 14) = 0

⇒ (x + 14)(x - 10) = 0

So, value of x = 10 or - 14

The value of x cannot be in negative so x = 10

So, width of the embankment = 10 m

**∴ The width (in m) of the embankment is 10 m.**

And the amount of soil dug out is equal to the volume of the well
